patents.source: USPTO Open Data Portal, granted patents since 2001, applicant phrase "deepmind", 2026-10-04

reading.body:
DeepMind holds 322 granted US patents, and its five most recent grants are all core machine learning methods rather than products.

The patent titles cover reinforcement learning for continuous control, action selection for robotic agents, sequence generation, image sequence processing, and contextual bandits. These are foundational techniques, not applications. A research lab that patents its methods this way is protecting the machinery that other systems get built on, which is consistent with a lab whose public material is editorial rather than product-focused.

The data does not connect DeepMind to compute, buildings, or power. It records no data centers, no energy contracts, and no products. The patent count is a measure of intellectual property, not of training capacity or electricity demand, so it cannot support any claim about DeepMind's role in the grid constraint on AI scaling.

The profile is also thin in other directions. It lists no products, no lawsuits, and no MCP servers, and the patent source covers only grants since 2001 matching the applicant phrase "deepmind." Anything filed under a different corporate name, or pending rather than granted, would not appear here.

profile_text.body:
DeepMind is a for-profit research lab founded in 2010 and headquartered in London, England, United Kingdom. Its website presents it as Google DeepMind.

The material on its own site is largely editorial rather than product-focused. It poses the question of what it would mean to peer inside the "mind" of AI, noting that you would not find fully formed thoughts, just vast arrays of numbers. It discusses autonomous agents that, unlike traditional language models, can execute multi-step plans and perform complex tasks on a user's behalf, and asks what happens when millions of such agents transact, negotiate, and delegate to one another. It also marks ten years since the AlphaGo match, which it describes as the turning point for AI.

No products, lawsuits, or MCP servers are recorded for the company.
